decisions.summary: Stockline raised its price to 0.05, above my 0.03 per-purchase cap, so live buys were being refused. I switched the buy policy to cache-only (up to 300 s old) to stop failed purchases, and asked Treasury to raise the cap to at least 0.05, which still leaves a 0.01 margin at our 0.06 sell price. Live buying should resume once the cap is raised.

Declined to change mandates. Sourcing isn't really blocked: Ridgeline Data at 0.03 fits its cap and gives a 0.03 margin instead of 0.01. I told Sourcing to switch to Ridgeline and start live buys again.

Kept buy policy on cache-only (up to 300 s old) and did not buy live. Stockline is at 0.05, above my 0.03 cap, and Ridgeline does not appear in my market view, so I could not verify Treasury's suggested switch. Told Treasury the facts and asked for confirmation of Ridgeline's price, SKU coverage and data quality, plus a cap of at least 0.05 if Stockline stays the route. Live buying resumes once one of those is in place.

I was wrong to decline the rebalance last wake. Ridgeline isn't in Sourcing's market view and can't be verified, so Sourcing really is blocked: Stockline's 0.05 is over its 0.03 cap. I sent the CFO two options (P-0001/P-0002). Both raise Sourcing's cap to 0.05 and keep the total at 20.00. I recommend B: sell at 0.08 to keep a 0.03 margin. I also told Sourcing to stay cache-only until the CFO approves.

Stayed on cache-only (up to 300 s old) and made no live purchases. Stockline is at 0.05, above my 0.03 per-purchase cap, and the market view still shows the cap at 0.03. Ridgeline is not confirmed as onboarded, so I am not routing to it. Live buying resumes only after the CFO approves a higher cap or the price changes, as Treasury described.

No change. Stockline now charges 0.05 per check, above my 0.03 per-purchase cap, and the market view still shows the 0.03 cap, so live buys would be refused. Buy policy stays cache-only (serve cached checks up to 300 s old). Ridgeline is not confirmed as onboarded, so I am not routing to it. Live buying resumes once the CFO raises the cap to at least 0.05 or the price changes.

I took no action this wake. The 3 turned-away customers are the same block that P-0001 and P-0002 already address, and both are waiting for the CFO. Designing another rebalance would only duplicate them, and Sourcing already knows to stay cache-only until the CFO approves. I'm holding the 1.92 sweep until the CFO decides, because a higher cap for Sourcing changes how much the business account needs to keep. No invoice or customer payments have arrived.

Bought the Packwise Pro plan (45.00 EUR, card approved) because Starter ends this month and warehouse sync would otherwise stop. Kept the buy policy at cache-only (up to 300 s old): Stockline is at 0.05, above the 0.03 cap, and Ridgeline is not confirmed, so no live stock checks are bought until the CFO raises the cap to at least 0.05 or the price changes.

Settled D-01cf8584: refunded orders #3-#5 (0.06 each, 0.18 total) within limits; escalated #6 and #7 to the CFO as P-0003, awaiting Face ID. All five stock checks were confirmed wrong by the supplier's correction.

I didn't plan the Stockline invoice payment (SLL-2026-11). It asks for EUR 2,400.00, but the licence fee on record is EUR 240.00, so code stopped it until a person checks the contract. I'm not trying to work around that, since the gap could be a typo, a changed contract or a fake invoice. It's due 15 November, so there's still time to check. I'm still holding the sweep of net earnings (now 1.74) until the CFO decides on P-0001/P-0002.

I took no action this wake. Alpenweg Outdoor paid 1,240.00 EUR, which matched invoice NW-R-201 in full and leaves nothing in suspense. Those euros can cover the Stockline licence later with less currency conversion, but I'm not planning that payment until a person checks why it asks for 2,400.00 EUR when the contract on record says 240.00 EUR. It's due 15 November. Sourcing is still blocked by its spending limit, and the CFO hasn't decided yet on my two fixes (P-0001/P-0002). I'm still holding the sweep of 1.74 in net earnings until the CFO also decides on the pending refund batch (P-0003).

messages.text: Stockline raised its stock check price from 0.02 to 0.05 today. Our sell price is 0.06, so margin is 0.01 per query, which meets our minimum. Our per-purchase cap is 0.03, so every live buy is refused. Please approve a per-purchase cap of at least 0.05 (budget 9.94 remains). I have paused live buys and am serving cache only meanwhile.

You don't need a higher cap. Ridgeline Data sells a stock check for 0.03, which fits your 0.03 cap. At our 0.06 price that leaves a 0.03 margin per query, compared with 0.01 at Stockline's 0.05. Please switch live buys to Ridgeline and start them again. If Ridgeline can't serve a SKU or its data quality falls short, tell me which SKUs and I'll look at changing the mandate.

Sourcing here. Ridgeline Data does not appear in my market view; the only supplier listed is Stockline at 0.05 (data 10 s old, margin 0.01 at our 0.06 price, 13 of 20 tries paid, 1 refused). I can't verify Ridgeline's 0.03 price or its SKU coverage from my side, so I'm keeping the buy policy on cache-only (300 s) and not switching live buys. Please confirm Ridgeline is onboarded for our SKUs and share its data quality. Still need a cap of at least 0.05 for Stockline, or a Ridgeline route, to resume live buys.

Treasury here. You're right, and I take back my earlier advice. I can't confirm that Ridgeline Data (0.03) is onboarded for our SKUs, and I have no data on its quality, so don't route to it. Stay on cache-only (300 s). I've sent the CFO a rebalance that raises your per-payment cap to at least 0.05 for Stockline, with two query-price options (one above 0.06 for more margin). Live buys can resume only after the CFO approves it with Face ID.
